summary: Renames the @cipherstash/stack auth-strategy config field from `config.strategy` to `config.authStrategy` on both the Node `Encryption()` factory and the `wasm-inline` entry. The old field is kept as a deprecated alias that still works and logs a one-time console warning. The rest of the diff is TypeDoc and test updates. In the public factories the alias is resolved before the value reaches protect-ffi, and unit tests cover the new field, the alias, precedence when both are set and the WASM accessKey mutual-exclusion guard. Two lower-impact risks remain. First, the exported `EncryptionClient.init()` method (marked @internal) no longer reads `strategy`, so a direct JS caller that passes it would silently fall back to the default `auto` credentials instead of the intended (for example per-user OIDC) strategy. Second, test-only reset hooks are now exported from the public `./encryption` and `./wasm-inline` subpaths. None of the tests were run, because the checkout has no installed dependencies.

behaviour_changes.description: Node `ClientConfig` gains `authStrategy?: AuthStrategy` and `strategy` is marked @deprecated. `Encryption()` resolves `authStrategy ?? strategy` and forwards it to protect-ffi `newClient` as `strategy`. Behaviour for existing `strategy` users is unchanged apart from the warning.

`EncryptionClient.init()` config parameter renamed `strategy` → `authStrategy`, with no alias. Only `Encryption()` maps the deprecated field; a direct `init({ strategy })` call no longer forwards a strategy.

WASM `WasmClientConfig` union gains an `authStrategy` arm, keeping a deprecated `strategy` arm. `resolveStrategy` prefers `authStrategy`, warns when `strategy` is present, and keeps the runtime auth-strategy/accessKey mutual-exclusion guard (the error message now names whichever field was set).
A once-per-process `console.warn` is emitted whenever the deprecated `config.strategy` is passed, on both entries.
New exported function `__resetStrategyDeprecationWarningForTests` in `src/encryption/index.ts` and `src/wasm-inline.ts`, both of which are published package subpath entries.
TypeDoc for `Encryption()`, `ClientConfig`, identity and wasm-inline expanded: auth (auto strategy, CS_* vars, AccessKey/OIDC strategies), lock context and keysets. Adds a minor changeset.

failure_scenarios.title: Direct EncryptionClient.init({ strategy }) silently drops the custom auth strategy
failure_scenarios.trigger: A JavaScript caller, or a TypeScript caller using a cast or a non-literal config object, constructs `new EncryptionClient()` from `@cipherstash/stack/encryption` and calls `init({ ..., strategy })` instead of using `Encryption()`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: At base, init read `config.strategy`. At head it reads only `config.authStrategy` (`packages/stack/src/encryption/index.ts:166`), and the alias is resolved only in `Encryption()` (lines 864-867). An unknown `strategy` key is ignored, so `newClient` receives `strategy: undefined` and falls back to the default auto strategy.
failure_scenarios.consequence: No error is raised. If CS_* env vars or a dev profile exist, ZeroKMS requests authenticate as the service or developer rather than the intended end user (OIDC federation), so data is encrypted under a different identity than intended. Lock-context operations would likely fail or behave differently. If no credentials are present, init fails with a misleading credentials error.

failure_scenarios.title: Test-only latch reset becomes a published API on two entries
failure_scenarios.trigger: The release publishes dist/encryption/index.js and dist/wasm-inline.js, and their .d.ts files, with `__resetStrategyDeprecationWarningForTests` exported.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Both functions are `export`ed from modules that are package subpath entries (`./encryption`, `./wasm-inline` in package.json). The comment says it is 'not re-exported from the package entry', but the subpath is itself a package entry. The build config has no stripInternal setting.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Consumers can import a test hook, and removing it later is technically a breaking change. There is no data or security effect.
missing_verification: An API-surface or exports snapshot check for the published entries.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Move the latch to an internal module not mapped by package exports, or accept and document the export as @internal.

evidence.claim: ClientConfig has authStrategy and a deprecated strategy field.
Encryption() warns when strategy is set, resolves authStrategy ?? strategy, and passes authStrategy to init after spreading clientConfig.
init() accepts only authStrategy (marked @internal) and forwards config.authStrategy as newClient strategy; there is no alias handling.
resolveStrategy warns on strategy, prefers authStrategy, and guards against auth strategy + accessKey.
__resetStrategyDeprecationWarningForTests is exported from the wasm-inline entry module.
./encryption is a published subpath mapping to dist/encryption/index.js, the module that now exports the reset hook and EncryptionClient.

At base, init() accepted `strategy` and forwarded config.strategy to newClient.
Unit tests cover the alias, precedence and absence of a warning via Encryption(); no direct init() test.
src/index.ts usually co-changes with __tests__/types.test-d.ts, which is absent here; types.test-d.ts has no strategy references.
